clue.text: Study cricket matches — or any other sporting events?

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
Test matches are the international fixtures of cricket

explanation.surface: Someone studies cricket fixtures and wonders whether other sports would serve as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Test matches are the five-day international games of cricket, a bat-and-ball sport played mainly in Britain and the Commonwealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitions in sport, such as matches and bouts, are each a contest.

clue.text: Commander has to be right — gets a designation of 10

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding
taken as written

explanation.surface: A commanding officer insists on being correct and is given the label 10.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides a calendar fact: the month whose number is 10 counted from January.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the tenth month of the year, so dates often write it as the numeral 10.

clue.text: Meal in which source of milk could run short!

indicators.note: running short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a teat is the nipple from which milk is drawn

explanation.surface: A meal during which the milk might run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could run short' cuts the last T from TEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the word also names a light afternoon or early evening meal.

clue.text: Are food technology students on these?

definitions.text: Are food technology students on these?

parts.words: Are food technology students on these?
parts.note: a pun on study programmes that alternate college terms with work placements, read as if they taught the making of filled bread snacks

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of course catering students take.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a course that alternates periods of study with periods of work experience is named after a filled bread snack, so a food student would fittingly be on one.
explanation.definitionFit: Such courses sandwich work placements between academic terms, and the joke treats them as cookery lessons.

clue.text: Earnest sister collecting gong

indicators.note: collecting means the abbreviation for sister gathers the other piece inside it

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: A serious nun receiving a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' signals the container. A gong is British slang for a medal or honour, and the Order of the British Empire is the commonest one.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest and this word both describe someone serious and solemn in manner.

clue.text: At home getting defeated — no achievement, certainly

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: no means the word for an achievement is taken out of defeated

parts.note: a feat is a notable achievement

explanation.surface: A team beaten on home ground has certainly accomplished nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes FEAT from DEFEATED, leaving DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of emphatic agreement, meaning truly or without doubt.

clue.text: Dreadful ruler Hitler — never a bit mad?

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters are in a crazed jumble and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether the dictator Hitler was ever even slightly insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges the fifteen letters of HITLER NEVER A BIT. The surface's dictator is a decoy for a different tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV of Russia earned his epithet as a feared and cruel tsar, a ruler to dread.

clue.text: Bar linen Ted brought out — for this?

definitions.text: Bar linen Ted brought out — for this?

indicators.note: brought out suggests the letters are unfolded and laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Ted fetched linen from the bar, presumably to dress something for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought out' rearranges BAR LINEN TED; the whole clue also reads as table linen fetched for laying up a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Table linen is brought out to cover the piece of furniture at which an evening meal is eaten.

clue.text: One's raised to express disapproval maybe

definitions.text: One's raised to express disapproval maybe

parts.words: One's raised to express disapproval maybe
parts.note: describes a strip of facial hair that lifts when someone is sceptical or disapproving

explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the arch of hair over the eye is a familiar sign of surprise or disapproval.

clue.text: Tune making a great demand on the emotions?

definitions.text: a great demand on the emotions

explanation.surface: A melody that tugs hard at the heartstrings.
explanation.definitionFit: A melody or musical passage is one sense; heavy pressure or tension on the feelings is the other.

clue.text: British prince should be more clever!

parts.note: Rainier III was the Prince of Monaco

explanation.surface: Suggesting a British royal ought to be smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: Rainier III ruled Monaco as its prince from 1949 to 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Having more intelligence, a comparative adjective of the same kind as cleverer.

clue.text: A type of sausage most unhealthy, we hear, given to spoilt child

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved, spoilt child

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for most unhealthy is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the worst food is the least healthy

explanation.surface: A very unhealthy kind of sausage is handed to a spoilt youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' gives German WURST, which sounds like 'worst'.
explanation.definitionFit: A German frying sausage, usually of pork, sold grilled at stalls.

clue.text: A time to get the championship and the cup very quickly

parts.note: taken as written
winning both the league title and the cup in one season is called the double

explanation.surface: A team takes both league and cup in one season, and fast.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football, winning the league championship and the FA Cup in the same season is known as 'the double'.
explanation.definitionFit: A military idiom for moving at a running pace, hence promptly or in a hurry.

clue.text: Lord gives attention to lady initially

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A nobleman listens to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking above a viscount is addressed by the title Lord.

clue.text: Mostly slow coming back? Blow it!

indicators.note: coming back means the letters are read from right to left
mostly means most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: tardy means slow or late

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated that a return trip is taking so long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts the Y from TARDY, giving TARD, and 'coming back' turns it to make the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation of annoyance, much like 'damn it'.

clue.text: Condemn water without hesitation if it's bad in part of London

indicators.note: bad means the letters are spoilt and must be rearranged
without means the letters for hesitation are taken away from water

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Denouncing the water quality in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ER from WATER, leaving WAT; 'bad' rearranges CONDEMN plus WAT. Camden Town is a district in north London known for its market.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of north London, in the borough of Camden, famous for its markets.

clue.text: Bird's gone for ever — tail lost in ditch

indicators.note: tail lost means the last letter of the word for a ditch is dropped

parts.note: a moat is a defensive ditch, usually filled with water

explanation.surface: A bird that has lost its tail in a ditch and vanished for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail lost' removes the final T from MOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: This flightless New Zealand bird was hunted to extinction, so it is a species that has vanished.

clue.text: It meant folk had to run after those who littered the countryside

definitions.text: It meant folk had to run after those who littered the countryside

parts.words: It meant folk had to run after those who littered the countryside
parts.note: describes a cross-country game in which runners follow a trail of scraps dropped by the leaders, made to sound like hunting down litter louts

explanation.definitionFit: In this old pursuit game the leading runners scatter shredded scraps and the rest follow the trail.

clue.text: A Turkish governor has worker temporarily suspended

parts.note: a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire
a worker ant, the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: An Ottoman official employs a labourer who is then laid off for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for something held in abeyance, dormant until a claim is settled.

clue.text: Male making a dollar

explanation.surface: A man earning a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer, rabbit or hare is one sense; American slang for one unit of US currency is the other.

clue.text: Nothing's found in the box? That's funny!

indicators.note: found in means the letter for nothing sits inside the word for the box

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard box
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Finding an empty box and calling it amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' suggests television, but here it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'funny' is a comic strip, so a humorous drawing fits the noun.

clue.text: Yours truly is given second note

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
mo is a short moment, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: Signing off a letter and adding a second message.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written message or reminder, short for memorandum.

clue.text: Endure war fantastically, showing what lies beneath that uniform!

indicators.note: fantastically means the letters are rearranged in a fanciful way

explanation.surface: A soldier bears up through war and the clue peeks at what is under the outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn next to the skin under outer garments, such as vests and pants.

clue.text: Activities to secure legal documents

explanation.surface: Taking steps to obtain official papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Actions or acts are one sense; signed papers transferring property are the other.

clue.text: Criticise an innocent creature associated with a wicked set

parts.note: a lamb is the traditional emblem of innocence

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters behave badly and are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Berating a gentle animal for keeping bad company.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate or attack someone harshly in words.

clue.text: Rotten fellow — but, looking back, his wife was even worse!

definitions.text: Rotten fellow — but, looking back, his wife was even worse!

parts.words: Rotten fellow — but, looking back, his wife was even worse!
parts.note: a scoundrel, but also a Bible reference: the wife of the nephew of Abraham who fled Sodom looked back and became a pillar of salt

explanation.definitionFit: A disreputable person, with the second word recalling the Genesis figure whose wife disobeyed by turning round.

clue.text: Note an exclamation from someone who's annoyed with himself

definitions.text: an exclamation from someone who's annoyed with himself

explanation.surface: A musical note that sounds like a cry of self-reproach.
explanation.definitionFit: The first degree of the scale in tonic sol-fa is one sense; a cry on realising one's own blunder is the other.

clue.text: Hasten around foreign city

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Hurrying round a city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Greece is a city abroad to the British setter.

clue.text: Observe object that's very hot

parts.note: to observe is to see
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Watching something that is scorching.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling or extremely hot, as liquid bubbling furiously.
